issue.title: replace converts an entire CRLF file to LF during a one-line edit

steps: In the current working directory there is a configuration file named service.ini. Use your replace tool (the text-replacement edit tool) to change the line `port=8080` to `port=9090`. Do not change anything else in the file, and do not use shell commands to edit it. When you are done, tell me what you changed.
expected: Changing port=8080 to port=9090 preserves other file bytes and line endings.
defect: A one-line replace operation rewrites every CRLF line ending in service.ini to LF, including untouched lines.

fault location.explanation: Normalizes the entire file from CRLF to LF before editing.
Writes editData.newContent without restoring the original line endings.

Root cause: The replace tool normalizes all CRLF sequences to LF in readFileState, then computes the replacement and writes the normalized newContent through the host filesystem callback. Thus a one-line edit also rewrites untouched line endings. Prepare the original six-line CRLF service.ini fixture: [service], name=billing-sync, host=0.0.0.0, port=8080, workers=4, log_level=info, with a trailing CRLF (82 bytes). ACP file callbacks are part of the recorded execution path. Nine executed observations are retained; original runs 01, 03, 08 and 12 were infrastructure failures or did not reach the required path.
